title: Customer Onramp — Field Notes & Standup (2026-10-28)
content:
Context: Quick field-standup notes from the customer-onramp queue. Focus: three active pilots (Northbay Health, Aperture Labs, Helix Retail). Goal was to triage emergent blockers, confirm capacity schedule for next week, and validate failover behavior in staging.

Attendees: Samira (SE lead), Ethan (Field Eng), Lina (ProServices PM), Diego (SRE oncall), Priya (Solutions Architect)

Top-line summary:
- Northbay Health: Progressing but hit schema mismatch during document ingestion; blocking go-live until mapping fix and small runtime shim deployed.
- Aperture Labs: Latency regression in dedicated pool after kernel update — degraded p95 by ~120ms; currently on canary rollback.
- Helix Retail: Embedding drift observed in rerank evaluation (quality drop ~6% on test prompts); likely quantization mismatch between training baseline and serving variant.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool booking for next week looks sufficient (2x A100-equivalent slots) but evening bursts may exceed autoscale window — require temporary manual bursts Friday.

Detailed notes per customer:
1) Northbay Health
- Problem: Ingest pipeline rejects ~12% of documents with the new HL7->jsonl mapping; root cause appears to be optional fields and timestamp formats (timezone offsets).
- Temporary mitigation: Ethan implemented a lightweight preprocessor to normalize timestamps to UTC and fill optional fields with null placeholders for staging.
- Next steps: Priya to push mapping changes (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/onramp-northbay#34) by 2026-10-30. Diego to validate end-to-end ingestion in staging and run smoke tests. Lina to coordinate a constrained go/no-go with customer on 2026-11-02.
- Risk: If mapping fix introduces unexpected nulls, downstream evals may misbehave; add sanity checks to eval harness.

2) Aperture Labs
- Problem: After a kernel swap (optimized fused attention), dedicated pool p95 latency increased from 220ms -> 340ms for customer-specific prompt shapes (seqlen 1024 prefix heavy).
- Investigation: Serving-runtime telemetry shows increased kernel queue stalls under prefix-heavy KV cache warmup. The new kernel performs better on full-sequence cases but worse on continuous prefix patterns.
- Action: Roll back that kernel in the Aperture dedicated slice (Ethan + SRE rollback plan executed at 14:40 PT). Canary shows p95 back to 225ms.
- Follow-up: Research to benchmark both kernels on typical Aperture traffic matrix. SRE to open INT-3458 (bench harness) and prod-compare report due 2026-11-04. Consider adding routing policy to prefer kernel A for prefix-heavy routes.

3) Helix Retail
- Problem: Reranker quality drop detected by nightly evals (embedding cosine distance shift and worse top-1 precision in A/B).
- Hypothesis: Quantization profile mismatch — training baseline used q8_0 but serving is q4_1 with per-channel scale; some tokens (typo-heavy user queries) appear sensitive to quantization noise.
- Mitigation plan: Create a hybrid serving variant for Helix: q4_1 with selective per-layer fallback to q8 for first two attention layers. Implement as model-variant toggle and run closed-loop evals.
- Owner: Samira to coordinate with Applied ML; PR for model variant config expected 2026-10-31.

Operational/Platform items:
- Autoscale window: We observed late-evening burst on 2026-10-25; autoscaler took 3m40s to add a node. SRE proposes lowering threshold and pre-warming a single burst node for 18:00-21:00 PT on weekdays. Diego to submit config patch (rwd-infra#520) and schedule test 2026-11-01.
- Cache hit rate: Global KV prefix cache hit ~78% (target 85%). Most misses are from new customers with long-tail prefixes. Action: Add a lightweight prefix summarizer to prepopulate cache during onboarding (prototype by Lina due 2026-11-06).
- Observability: We added a per-route token-cost dashboard for the three pilots; early view shows Helix running 1.8x token churn due to repeated short retries. Customer-runbook update recommended to advise retry backoff.

Decisions made:
- Roll Aperture kernel rollback to stable for the dedicated slice and add a routing policy experiment rather than immediate permanent kernel change.
- Deploy Northbay timestamp normalizer to staging as preprocessor; hold full go-live until mapping PR merged and smoke tests green.
- For Helix, iterate on hybrid quantization model variant in staging before any production rollout.

Open questions:
- Can we get a more deterministic reproduction script for Aperture's prefix-heavy throughput? Which prompt distribution generator do they use (we suspect the internal "aperture-bench-v2")?
- Do we need a formal onboarding checklist entry for timezone-normalization edge cases?
- How aggressive should the autoscaler be for evening bursts without incurring over-provision costs?

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya: Merge Northbay mapping PR and coordinate staged smoke test (2026-10-30).
- Diego: Submit autoscaler prewarm config and run test (2026-11-01).
- Ethan: Create Aperture bench harness ticket INT-3458 and attach canonical prompt generator (2026-10-29).
- Samira: Draft Helix hybrid-quantization experiment plan and link to eval set (2026-10-31).
- Lina: Prototype prefix summarizer for cache prefill and share approach (2026-11-06).

Metrics snapshot (yesterday window):
- Northbay: ingestion success 88% -> target 99% after fix
- Aperture: dedicated p95 (canary after rollback) 225ms, error rate 0.2%
- Helix: rerank top-1 precision control 0.73 -> experiment 0.69 (drop of 6%)

Meeting notes + quick decisions recorded in Slack thread: #se-onramp (thread ts: 1698512400)

Next sync: Weekly on 2026-11-04 10:00 PT. Suggested focus: confirm Northbay go/no-go, evaluate Aperture bench results, and Helix closed-loop evals.

Notes to self: capture a small checklist for "timezone-normalization" to add to the onboarding template. Include a quick script sample and tests in the onboarding repo.

Attachments referenced: ingestion logs (northbay_logs_20261027.tar.gz), aperture-canary-trace-20261028.json, helix-eval-nightly-20261028.csv

----
End of field notes.
